Tessa — forwarding what happened when I sent the consolidated invite to our EU partner. Their calendar showed the meeting at 19:00 CEST instead of 20:00 CEST (one hour earlier).

Forwarded message (snippet):
> From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
> Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:05:00 +02:00
> To: partner-eu@example.com
> Subject: Redwood demo — Thu 11:00 PDT / 20:00 CEST
>
> (attached redwood-demo-20270418.ics)

When I inspected the .ics, the DTSTART was listed without a TZ identifier (i.e., a "floating" time). If someone forwards that invite from Gmail or imports it into Outlook, the client can treat it as local time and shift it incorrectly. I saved the forwarded message to a .eml and attached it for debugging.

Recommendation: generate explicit TZ-aware invites (VTIMEZONE block) or send three separate invites (PDT/CEST/AEST). Also add UTC offset in the event title — e.g., "11:00 PDT (18:00 UTC) / 20:00 CEST" — so recipients can sanity-check.

Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
